citation.authors: García-Suárez PC, Rentería I, Moncada-Jiménez J, Fry AC, Jiménez-Maldonado A
citation.title: Acute Systemic Response Of BDNF, Lactate and Cortisol to Strenuous Exercise Modalities in Healthy Untrained Women

population.description: Seventeen physically active healthy female undergraduates (Table 1: age 20.0 +/- 0.9 yr, BMI 23.0 +/- 2.6 kg/m2, weight 58.1 +/- 8.0 kg, predicted VO2max 38.1 +/- 5.6 mL/kg/min, MAP 183.5 +/- 29.4 W); free of cardiac or respiratory problems; menstrual cycle phase varied between follicular and luteal. The paper calls them healthy; no glucose test.

protocols.name: rest_before_gxt
protocols.description: Seated rest before the graded cycle test, 11:00-13:00 (clock hour assumed). Minute 0 is the baseline antecubital blood draw (immediately after the body-composition assessment); resting blood pressure was recorded 5 min after it (minute 5). The paper says nothing of food before the visit except 'refrain from eating or drinking 2-h before' the body-composition test, with no contents: fed state unknown, so the arm starts from typical values with no meal. No exercise is entered.

findings.description: Resting systolic blood pressure before the GXT, 5 min after the baseline blood draw (minute 5, window one minute); fed state before the visit not described (mean of the GXT visit, n = 17, as printed)

location.quote: Mean baseline SBP (GXT = 119.9 ± 19.9 mmHg vs. HIIT = 116.6 ± 10.5 mmHg

findings.description: Resting diastolic blood pressure before the GXT, 5 min after the baseline blood draw (minute 5, window one minute); fed state before the visit not described (mean of the GXT visit, n = 17, as printed)

left_out.what: Blood lactate before and after the GXT (Results: pre 1.8 +/- 0.9, post 12.6 +/- 3.1 mMol/l, finger capillary, 'final stage's immediate' value): the test ran 'until participants reached volitional exhaustion', so each rider ended at her own stage (MAP 183.5 +/- 29.4 W, Table 1) and the exercise cannot be written as one schedule; and 'two participants were considered outlier and were excluded from the analysis for BLa', a group chosen by the lactate itself (n = 15 is my arithmetic)

Resting lactate before the GXT (1.8 +/- 0.9) and before the HIIT (1.8 +/- 1.0 mMol/l): the state before the visit is not described (no fast stated, no meal contents), and the same two outliers were excluded

HIIT session (30-s bouts at 90% MAP with 90-120 s active recovery at 40% MAP; warm-up length and number of bouts not printed, so the schedule cannot be written; each rider's MAP differs) and its post-session lactate 16.3 +/- 2.8 mMol/l, baseline SBP 116.6 +/- 10.5 and DBP 74.5 +/- 9.3 mmHg (the same people, a second visit), distance and work

Serum cortisol pre 13.2 +/- 1.2 and post 19.1 +/- 0.9 ug/dl, and heart rate pre 79.4 +/- 2.4, immediately post 190.5 +/- 1.6, 60-s recovery 165.3 +/- 2.0 bpm (Results): printed 'regardless of the trial', pooled over the GXT and HIIT sessions, not for the GXT alone
Per-trial cortisol, BDNF and cortisol:BDNF means and SDs (Supplemental Table 2, not in the full text)
Serum BDNF (pre/post, d effect sizes in text)
Rating of perceived exertion, total distance and work, peak HR by trial (RPE, GXT 15.8 +/- 2.3; distance, kJ)
Predicted VO2max from an indirect method (Table 1), MAP and body composition: descriptive, used only for population
